page.overview:
Who is Abigail Housman?

In 1658, Abigail was approached at her cottage by Viscount de Ablo, a demonic agent of Mephisto traveling under the name "Stephen Hart," who demanded that she hand over the Brighthold. When she refused, de Ablo used the Gorath Stone to lay a wasting curse upon Christ's Crown, withering its fields and livestock and spreading sickness through the town, until the desperate villagers began searching for someone to blame. Hoping to save her community, Abigail opened the Brighthold and cast a summoning spell for aid, inadvertently drawing a time-displaced, human-form Blackheart from the future, bound to her will by her own magic. Recognizing the Brighthold's power and sensing a connection to his own destiny, the demon adopted the name "Gabriel," came to believe Abigail to be his mortal mother, and remained at her side as they translated the grimoire and used its spells to comfort the sick, including a young girl named Constance.

As de Ablo continued to inflame the town's fears, the people of Christ's Crown turned against Abigail, branding her a witch and blaming her secret learning for the curse afflicting them. On a stormy night, her betrothed Malcolm, misled by de Ablo, came to her door claiming his sister needed her care and led Abigail up Christ's Crown Hill into the hands of a waiting mob, where she was publicly executed as a witch while Gabriel stayed behind to comfort the dying Constance. With Abigail's death, Blackheart's full demonic power returned; he confronted de Ablo on the hill, revealed his true nature and left the viscount broken amid the hellfire-scorched earth before departing with the Brighthold.

Later accounts identified Abigail's murder on Christ's Crown Hill as the first crime in a chain of atrocities that saturated the site with evil and ultimately allowed Mephisto to gestate Blackheart there, a role the demon acknowledged centuries later while confessing under the human name Gabriel Housman.
